Diagram contrasting a bounded control system with bounded circularity. Internal loops of extraction, manufacture, use and recovery are shown operating within a closed system boundary, while energy inputs, material loss, emissions and degraded outputs cross the boundary. The figure highlights that internal circularity does not necessarily produce ecological reciprocity when wider exchanges and affected agents remain outside the model.

Diagram showing phased scaffolding as overlapping physical and digital life cycles. Organic entities arranged around a circular field pass through phases of initial scaffold, growth, stabilisation, decline, death, decay and re-emergence. A parallel digital layer shows parameters and modules being introduced, monitored, renegotiated, deprecated and reborn. Cross-links identify reciprocity, resource exchange, sensing, care and parameter evolution.

Diagram showing a sequence of material states as permission structures for interaction. Distinct states such as solid, plastic-like, liquid and additional speculative intermediate states selectively permit, inhibit or condition activities including global shape change, local property variation, healing, texture formation and exchange. The figure emphasises that a material state governs which relationships can act, and helps prevent one interaction from overriding the rest.
